title: 2024 AMC 10B Problem 8
statement: Let \(N\) be the product of all the positive integer divisors of \(42.\) What is the units digit of \(N?\)

solutions.text: Since \(42 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 7\) has \((1+1)^3 = 8\) divisors, we can pair each divisor with its complement, so \(N = 42^{\frac{8}{2}} = 42^4.\) Only the units digit matters, and \(2^4 = 16\) ends in \(6,\) so \(42^4\) does too. Therefore, the answer is D.
hints: A number with \(d\) divisors has divisor product equal to itself raised to the \(\tfrac{d}{2}\) power
